Heads up: this picture is 76 days old (last transaction 2026-03-28), so treat what follows as a snapshot, not a live read.

As of that date, the credit card goal needs £6,500 more to reach £8,000. With a deadline of 2027-01-01, that's roughly 9 months away from now — meaning the goal requires around £722 a month to land on time. Free cash flow as of the snapshot was £513 a month. That's a gap of roughly £209 a month between what the goal needs and what the data shows available.

With only 7 transactions across 87 days, the spending picture is thin — not enough to build reliable cluster-level patterns. What is clear: fixed costs are consuming the vast majority of income, with housing alone at £780 a month. That compression is what's creating the shortfall against the £722 pace.

The Value Map is blank. Without knowing which spending categories you'd trade off against the goal, there's no clean lever to size here — the system didn't produce one. The fastest way to change that is to tell me where you'd be willing to cut.

[CTA:supply_input]I'll fill in my Value Map so you can find the lever[/CTA]

— C.
